title: West Hollywood Offers Free Bike Lights to Residents for Safer Night Cycling on Santa Monica Boulevard - NewsBreak
text:
2 hours ago The City of West Hollywood and the West Hollywood Bicycle Coalition will hold Operation Firefly on November 25, 2025. The event will run from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. on both sides of Santa Monica Boulevard, east of N. San Vicente Boulevard. The purpose is to improve cycling safety by giving free bike lights to cyclists for better visibility at night.
Cyclists who bring their bikes can receive free lights while supplies last. The event will also offer water and other items. City staff will share information about local mobility projects and the use of bike lights. Assistance will be available in English and Spanish.
The event will inform attendees about California Vehicle Code § 21201(d). This law requires bikes used at night to have a white front light visible from 300 feet and certain reflectors. These rules are intended to make cyclists more visible and reduce accidents.
Studies show that bike lights can lower the risk of injury. For example, a 2013 Danish study found that using bike lights, including during the day, can reduce injury collisions by 19% to 47%.
Residents can learn more about the event or city mobility projects on the city’s website or by contacting city staff. The city provides updates through social media, email newsletters, and a public calendar. Accessibility services are available for people who are Deaf or hard of hearing.
